column1: # Salt knowledge: which atoms are cations, which may take the charge, which are acidic, and which whole
# components are known species.  Read by chython/chemistry/_tables.py, applied by chython/chemistry/_salts.py.
# TWO COLUMNS, TWO QUESTIONS.  `match` is HOW a row is recognized; `klass` is WHAT the row is.  A pass
# selects rows by `klass`, never by `match` -- which is what makes a new class invisible to a pass that
#   embed    SMARTS       embedding; the `:1` atom is the one the row is about
#   whole    SMILES       key equality against the WHOLE component
# Neither mechanism can express the other's question honestly: `[M;*:1]` would need 186 SMILES rows, and
# tartaric acid every hydrogen count spelled out as SMARTS.
#   metal_cation      embed   split_salts (the cation); decompose_salts, but only when the component IS
#                             that one atom -- a lone [Na+].  All 93 metals `[M]` accepts qualify.
#   charge_acceptor   embed   split_salts (the atom that keeps the electron pair)
#   protic_acid       embed   decompose_salts (the acid_salt tag), fix_salt_charges (the proton source)
#   metal_protic      embed   fix_salt_charges ONLY, and only when every free metal is s-block -- a site a
#                             reducing metal opens and no acid table calls an acid
#   the fourteen species classes  whole   decompose_salts
# A SPECIES ROW IS COMPARED BY `format(component, '!s')` -- the canonical SMILES with stereo disabled,
# after `thiele()` on both sides.  Stereo is out because a row names a CONSTITUTION: whether the tartrate
# is L, D or meso does not change that it is the counterion.  `thiele()` is in because the writer writes
# what is stored, so a Kekule toluene and an aromatic one are otherwise two different strings.  NOT
# `standardize()`: that is a repair the caller did not ask for, so a mis-drawn nitric acid needs
# `standardize()` first or a row of its own.
# A CONJUGATE IS NOT A ROW.  `decompose_salts` neutralizes before it matches, so `[Cl-]` is `Cl` and
# `CC([O-])=O` is acetic acid by the time the key is taken.  Only a species that cannot be neutral gets
# its own row: `salts:choline` is `quaternary_ammonium` and has nowhere to put the charge.
# A SPECIES THAT IS BOTH SOLVENT AND BASE IS TABULATED AS THE BASE.  `salts:pyridine` is `amine_base` and
# not a solvent class: as a solvent class it would read pyridine hydrochloride as hydrochloric acid, while
# as a base that record answers with both components as candidate parents, which a caller can reject.
# `charges` IS THE OVERCHARGE GUARD AND ONLY THE `metal_cation` ROW HAS ONE.  A cation cutting k bonds ends
# at charge+k; the row lists every value that is allowed to be, and the whole atom is refused before
# anything is cut -- all-or-nothing, never a partially split molecule.
# `order` IS THE ACIDITY RUNG AND ONLY A `protic_acid` OR `metal_protic` ROW HAS ONE.  Low is more acidic;
# rows sharing a value are tied, and a tie is resolved by canonical order and logged rather than by file
# position.  ONE SCALE FOR BOTH CLASSES, because `fix_salt_charges` ranks them in one pool: a carboxylic
# acid beside an alcohol and one sodium gives the carboxylate, rung 4 against rung 6.
# WATER AND ALCOHOL ARE NOT ACIDS, THEY ARE WHAT A FREE S-BLOCK METAL REDUCES.  `CCN.CCO` is a mixture and
# `CCO` is no acid site, so `decompose_salts` reads neither as a salt and a hydrate stays droppable;
# `CCO.[Na]` is sodium ethoxide, because sodium does not stand beside a hydroxyl.  That distinction is the
# whole of `metal_protic`.  Beryllium is the one s-block metal outside it, not reducing water.
# EVERY AZOLE BUT TETRAZOLE IS ABSENT.  Below sulfonamide's rung an N-H needs a hydride or an
# organolithium, and a metal drawn beside one is reagent chemistry.  An acid with no row refuses, logs, and
# surfaces as a `charges_undrawn` tag -- the count of those refusals is what would justify a row.
# There is no `elements` column: `pattern` already names the elements a row applies to, and `keep=['Na']` is

column7: any of the 93 metals `[M]` accepts, at any charge.  Generality is safe because every bond is cut or none is: see _salts.py

nitrate, drawn charge-separated as standardize() leaves it
a terminal halogen or oxygen: halide, hydroxide, alkoxide
alkoxide, thiolate, silanolate drawn with the metal bonded.  The `[M]` is the row: without it the pattern is true of diethyl ether

column7: nitric, drawn charge-separated as standardize() leaves it
sulfinic acid.  The sulfonic row above is `z5`, which this S is not
thioacid, dithioacid, xanthic acid, dithiocarbamic acid.  Thioacetic acid is a rung optimistic here, which costs a tie broken the wrong way when one component holds two sites
HF HCl HBr HI: the unbonded halogen holding its hydrogen
tetrazole 2H: standardize() converges no mobile hydrogen, so both tautomers get a row

maleic and fumaric -- one row, the key being taken with stereo disabled
tartaric, any stereoisomer, for the same reason

pyridine, an amine base: as a solvent class it would read pyridine hydrochloride as hydrochloric acid
